newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Navy shoots down missile with a missile.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Navy shoots down missile with a missile.

text.p: The U.S. Navy said it shot down a missile with another missile high over New Mexico on Friday in a successful initial test of a new infra-red targeting system designed to defend against missile attack.

The Navy said at the Pentagon that one of its "Standard" missiles containing a new heat-seeker in the nose destroyed an older "Lance" target missile at an altitude of more than 40,000 feet (12,000 metres) above White Sands Missile Range.

Both the Standard missile, used on Navy ships as a defense against attacking aircraft and other ships, and the new heat-seeker are produced jointly by Raytheon Co and the Hughes Missile Systems unit of General Motors Corp.
"It was a successful first try, the first time that the Navy has done this," said Lt. Greg Geisen, a Navy spokesman at the Pentagon.
The downing occurred at 8:32 a.m. MST (1532 GMT) and was part of the ongoing U.S. military effort to develop a defense against so-called theater ballistic missiles.
Both missiles were launched from White Sands. The Lance traveled about 250 miles (400 km) before it was hit by the Standard.
Geisen said the new Standard system would undergo further testing and current plans were to begin deploying the system aboard ships beginning in 1999.
The first guided missile cruisers scheduled to receive the new Standards are the Lake Erie and Port Royal, which have home ports at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii.

The Clinton administration and Pentagon earlier scrapped former President Ronald Reagan's dream of a costly "Star Wars" umbrella defense of the United States against massive missile attack. Instead, it is working actively on a less-ambitious initial system to protect troops and bases from attack.

Congressional Republicans are pressing the administration for a commitment to deploy a more elaborate Star Wars-type defense early in the next century, but the Pentagon says the cost would be too high unless it is warranted by a new offensive threat.
